yesterday_lede: We hold the clock at 84.1 seconds, with the biggest shift coming from a new human bird‑flu case and a coordinated fridge‑cyberattack in Europe.

chair.lede: The clock moves to 83.5 seconds, 0.5 closer to midnight than yesterday: ebola evacuation adds a fresh bio‑risk.
body: The evacuation of a British healthcare worker with Ebola from the Democratic Republic of Congo introduces a new cross‑border biological threat that was not covered by the baseline or existing pressures.
Climate adaptation funding shortfalls reported by the UN and Reuters deepen the existing climate‑extreme pressure, reflecting a worsening gap between needs and resources.
Multiple reports of cyberattacks on French blood‑bank systems expand the AI‑related cyber risk, prompting an increase to the fake‑alert pressure.

experts.say: No new nuclear weapons development, test, treaty change or safety incident appears; the IAEA reports are routine monitoring and programme updates, not new risks.
Reports that rich countries are falling far short on climate adaptation funding indicate a worsening of the existing adaptation shortfall pressure.
A British healthcare worker evacuated from the Democratic Republic of Congo with Ebola indicates a new cross‑border case, adding a fresh bio‑risk beyond the existing anthrax and bird‑flu pressures.

Recent reports of cyberattacks on French blood bank systems (headlines 9 and 13) show new threats to critical health infrastructure, expanding the AI‑related cyber risk beyond the previously noted fake emergency alerts.
No new war, treaty collapse, or major geopolitical shift reported; headlines discuss aid cuts, diplomatic statements, and missile launches that reflect ongoing tensions already accounted for.
